summary: The software-arch outline is structurally sound across all five judged axes and is approved. Every chapter sits at design-decision altitude (no infra/distributed-systems internals, no ML); ch-08 and ch-06/07 explicitly defend that altitude rather than drifting into ops. The deps[] graph is acyclic and honest — no chapter depends on a later one, and the foundations->boundaries->topology->contracts->consistency->evolution->capstone spine is correctly serialized, with the aggregate-as-seed (ch-03) preceding both saga (ch-06) and CQRS/ES (ch-07). Granularity at 10 chapters is a clean cut of the 9 content steps + lab, and both stated merges/splits are grounded in the excerpts themselves (verified: cockburn-hexagonal and martin-clean-arch both assert Clean=Hexagonal=Onion; young-cqrs-es's load-bearing thesis is that CQRS/ES are optional/independent, justifying ch-07's split). Source backing is fully verified: all 21 distinct excerpt slugs the outline cites exist on disk, there are zero orphan excerpts (every library file is consumed by at least one chapter), and spot-checks of 10 excerpts confirm the cited sources genuinely support the claims, with the gap-log hedges (Cockburn .com mirror, Fielding gbiv.com mirror, Helland Queue 403, Sagas-1987 image-only) honestly reproduced in the outline. No blocker or major issues found. Three minor findings are listed below for the planner to optionally fold in at authoring time. Findings by severity: 0 blocker, 0 major, 3 minor.

findings.issue: Concept 3 ('API-style selection as a trade-off: REST/HTTP vs gRPC vs GraphQL') cites only [[fielding-rest]]. But the library marks gRPC/GraphQL as *synthesis inside* fielding-rest (excerpt L8, L44-48), not verbatim primary sources, and both insights.md (L50) and COLLECTION-PLAN gap log (L58) say to 'promote [GraphQL/gRPC] to a standalone excerpt only if the outline gives API-style selection its own chapter' — which ch-05 effectively does. The cited source exists and supports the claim, so this is not a fabricated citation, but the trigger condition the library set for itself has now been met and is unaddressed.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) have the ch-05 read.md explicitly label the gRPC/GraphQL comparison as synthesis-level trade-off context (not primary-quoted), matching the excerpt's own marking, or (b) flag to the librarian to spin out a dedicated gRPC/GraphQL excerpt now that API-style selection has its own chapter. Option (a) is lower-cost and preserves the verbatim discipline the per_chapter_format promises.

findings.issue: ch-08 bundles the stability/resilience toolkit (concepts 1-4, all from [[nygard-release-it]]) with observability-as-architecture (concept 5, sourced from [[richards-ford-fundamentals]] + [[nygard-release-it]]). The resilience material is tightly coherent and well-sourced, but observability is a thinner, somewhat distinct concern riding on one shared concept; it risks being underdeveloped relative to the circuit-breaker/bulkhead/timeout core, or stretching the chapter's single-topic coherence.
findings.suggestion: Keep ch-08 as one chapter (a split is not warranted on current source volume), but in read.md tie observability explicitly to the resilience spine — frame 'what must be observable' as derived from the critical architecture characteristics and from where breakers/bulkheads define the blast radius, so it reads as one arc rather than two stapled concerns. No outline change required.

findings.issue: ch-06 concept 6 names 'CDC log-tailing' as one of the two outbox relay mechanisms. CDC sits near the infra boundary the course explicitly excludes; presented as a relay *option* it is legitimately at design altitude, but it is the single concept in the outline most at risk of drifting into broker/connector internals during authoring.
findings.suggestion: At authoring time, keep CDC vs polling-publisher strictly as a design-decision trade-off (reliability/latency/operational-cost of each relay choice) and do not descend into Debezium/Kafka-Connect mechanics. A one-line authoring guardrail in the chapter note would lock this in; no structural change needed.

strengths: Dependency graph is fully acyclic and honest: verified ch-01->ch-02->ch-03->ch-04->ch-05, ch-06 deps [ch-03,ch-05], ch-07 deps [ch-06], ch-08 deps [ch-06], ch-09 deps [ch-04,ch-08], ch-10 deps [ch-09,ch-07]; no forward dependency anywhere.

Zero orphan excerpts and zero phantom citations: all 21 distinct cited slugs map 1:1 to the 21 files in excerpts/, and every library file is consumed by at least one chapter — the source library is exactly covered.

Both merge/split decisions are grounded in the primary sources, not editorial convenience: the ch-03 hexagonal+clean+aggregates merge is backed by cockburn-hexagonal (L38-40) and martin-clean-arch (L40-42) both stating 'same idea, three names', and the ch-07 CQRS/ES split is backed by young-cqrs-es's explicit 'independent, optional, scope-tightly' thesis.

The trade-off spine is operationalized as a fixed per-chapter move (introduce pattern, then price it as a bet — what it keeps cheap vs makes expensive), which matches both the First Law in the sources and the learner's trade-off-native framing.

Doc-vs-reality myths are mapped chapter-by-chapter against the COLLECTION-PLAN reconciliation table, and the gap-log hedges (mirror sources, 403, image-only PDF) are reproduced honestly in the outline rather than papered over.

Every content chapter lands at least one concept back on the learner's production sales agent, and ch-10 is correctly scoped as a single capstone lab that exercises the whole toolkit into a real ADR + C4 design memo.
